after: The published reaction coordinate \(\omega\) is the isomerising Ala--Pro peptide-bond torsion~\cite{Q}. An umbrella window is a simulation biased towards a chosen value of this angle. The reported audit of the frozen input archive found omega-only biases in the enzyme inputs labelled in: their listed bias acts on this peptide torsion alone. Most inputs labelled out additionally restrain the Phe113 side-chain torsion and apply an upper distance wall~\cite{archive}. The distance joins the centre of mass of the substrate proline-ring atoms to a single combined centre of mass of the phenyl-ring atoms of Phe60 and Phe113. Here pooled means that the atoms from both phenyl rings enter that combined centre, rather than defining a separate distance to each ring. The upper wall adds a penalty when this distance exceeds its prescribed limit; the Phe113 torsion restraint instead penalises departure from its prescribed side-chain angle. Wild-type out has a window at zero \(\omega\) without either auxiliary bias; mutant out sets omit that window and use a Phe113 torsion-restraint stiffness different from that in the remaining wild-type out windows. Stiffness here describes the strength of that torsional penalty. These are archived input differences, not demonstrated production use or physical bias. Designed conditioning and undocumented protocol variation remain possible explanations.
